title: private-deployments-weekly-2026-05-25
content:
Private Deployments - Engineering Weekly
Date: 2026-05-25
Author: Aisha Khan (eng-private-deployments)
Status: in_review

Summary
- Sprint/weekly sync + standup highlights for the private deployments team. Focus this week: VPC install fixes, on-prem agent stability, and two customer escalations (CorpX and MediSys).
- Main blocker: CorpX network policy + MTU mismatch causing heartbeat loss in k8s clusters.
- Secondary blocker: MediSys air-gapped install failing on HSM integration step (KMS handshake timeout).

Attendees
- Aisha Khan (owner)
- Ethan Park
- María Gomez
- Liam O'Connor
- Marcus Li (SRE - joined for CorpX escalation)
- Customer Success: Priya Shah (joined parts)

Standup notes (by person)
- Aisha: Coordinated CorpX escalation with SRE and CS. Filed PD-1423 to track MTU investigation. Working on deployable workaround (proxy MTU clamp) to test in CorpX staging. Blocked by waiting on CorpX infra change window (they propose Tue 5/26).
- Ethan: On-prem agent v0.9.4 rollout - finished canary internally; observed rare OOM in agent-service when KV cache grows on long sessions. Repro steps and heap dump attached to PR-487. Plan: limit KV size per session and evict LRU entries; will ship hotfix (v0.9.5) by EOD 5/27.
- María: Packaging updates for air-gapped installs. Worked with infra to create an offline bundle for MediSys. Currently stuck on HSM libraries (vendor-signed binaries) signing mismatch. Opening vendor support ticket tomorrow.
- Liam: Telemetry + logging improvements for install flow. Added clearer failure codes for KMS/HSM handshake and wrote a small script to capture libcalls on handshake failure. Will coordinate with María on reproducing locally.

Customer escalations / blockers
1) CorpX (enterprise, Dedicated -> Private migration)
   - Symptom: Nodes intermittently lose heartbeat, pods restart; errors show "connection reset by peer" in runtime logs.
   - Investigation notes: SRE Marcus verified MTU differences between customer VPC overlay and our deployed infra. Large token payloads + iptables overlay exceeding MTU leads to fragmentation and drops.
   - Temporary mitigations tried: reduced batch sizes; prefix compression; not sufficient.
   - Action items: Aisha to coordinate CorpX change window (Tue 5/26) for MTU/overlay updates; Marcus to test MTU clamp in staging; Ethan to prepare v0.9.5 with smaller default batch/kv limits in case fragmentation continues. JIRA: PD-1423.
   - Customer impact: degraded throughput and occasional timeouts for inference requests; CS escalated to Tier 2.

2) MediSys (regulated healthcare, on-prem air-gapped)
   - Symptom: Air-gapped installer fails at HSM/KMS handshake step (timeout ~60s) - install rolls back.
   - Investigation notes: Vendor HSM library version mismatch (customer has HSM fw 3.1, our bundle expects 3.3). Binary signing and library checks fail.
   - Workaround: Manual vendor library drop-in was successful in one test machine; not acceptable at scale.
   - Action items: María to open vendor support and request back-compat libs; create a validated offline bundle with both lib sets; Liam to add clearer error messages and recovery guide in runbook. JIRA: PD-1399.
   - Customer impact: install delay, project go-live at risk for June window. CS requested weekly updates.

Operational work / infra
- On-prem agent hotfix (v0.9.5): target EOD 5/27. Hotfix scope: enforce KV cache ceiling, add graceful eviction, memory limits for agent-service. Owner: Ethan.
- Install runbook updates: add HSM troubleshooting section, `hsm-lib-version-check` step, and offline bundle validation checklist. Owner: Liam + María. Target: 5/29.
- Telemetry: add metric 'install.hsm.handshake_duration_ms' and 'agent.kv.evictions_total' to help correlate incidents. Owner: Liam.

Sprint items & priority this week
- P0: CorpX MTU mitigation + deployable workaround (Aisha, Marcus)
- P0: on-prem agent stability hotfix v0.9.5 (Ethan)
- P1: air-gapped offline bundle with vendor libs for MediSys (María)
- P1: Runbook/Docs updates for HSM/KMS and install troubleshooting (Liam + María)
- P2: Add test harness for large-token sessions to reproduce fragmentation scenarios (Ethan + SRE)

Meeting notes (syncs during the week)
- Tue 5/26 10:00am - CorpX escalation call: confirmed maintenance window Tue 5/26 22:00 UTC. Marcus to run MTU clamp test at 22:15; Aisha to be on standby. Outcome: staging test passed with clamp; production test scheduled.
- Wed 5/27 2:00pm - Hotfix planning: decision to ship 0.9.5 as hotfix with config toggle (enable-eager-eviction=false by default). Rollout plan: canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% over 24h. Ethan to coordinate rollout on 5/28.
- Thu 5/28 11:00am - Vendor call (MediSys HSM vendor) scheduled; María to drive.

Notes / open questions
- Should we add an automatic MTU-detection step in the installer that warns if overlay MTU < recommended? Pros: catches issues early. Cons: false positives across providers. Recommend: implement heuristic + opt-in enforcement. (Aisha to prototype)
- For air-gapped bundles, do we maintain multiple vendor lib sets as supported or require vendors to provide a compatibility shim? Need policy decision from product/legal for supported third-party binary distribution. (Raised to product-security)

Action items (owner, due)
- Aisha: Coordinate production mtU change window confirmation & post-mortem writeup (due 2026-05-29).
- Ethan: Ship agent v0.9.5 with KV ceiling + eviction and create rollout plan (due 2026-05-27).
- María: Vendor support ticket for MediSys HSM libs + build offline bundle (due 2026-05-28).
- Liam: Runbook updates + telemetry metrics instrumentation (due 2026-05-29).
- Marcus: Run MTU clamp test in CorpX production window and collect packet captures (due 2026-05-26).

Attachments / artifacts
- PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/private-deployments/pull/487 (agent heap dump + proposed fixes)
- JIRA: PD-1423 (CorpX MTU), PD-1399 (MediSys HSM)
- Runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PD/Private+Deployments+Runbook
- Slack thread: #private-deployments (CorpX escalation)

Quick retrospective notes
- The new KV cache growth uncovered gaps in memory-pressure testing for long-lived sessions; we need a synthetic test harness to simulate long-running chat sessions.
- Air-gapped packaging remains the slowest part of installs due to external vendor binaries and signing. Consider engaging a vendor-compatibility program (product + partnerships).

Next sync
- Weekly sync: Mon 2026-06-01 09:30am PT (regular time)
- CorpX post-prod test retrospective: Wed 2026-05-27 11:00am PT

Notes to self
- Save packet captures and heap dumps in /shared_artifacts/private-deployments/2026-05-25/ (Ethan/Marcus)
- Remind CS to set expectations for MediSys on timing and escalate to sales if go-live slips.

End of notes
